label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: A marketing signup dialog (email and phone for texts) popped up over the home page and blocked my click on a product link; I had to find and close it first.

After adding to cart, the cart dialog opened with Checkout Now, Remove and Increase quantity disabled and an empty subtotal; with no loading message I did not know if the add worked until I re-read the page.
Product page said Ships in 6-8 weeks while other text on the page says ready to ship and in-stock; no clear stock status, so I could not tell if the item was truly in stock.
Many links and images have unclear names: repeated Product Image labels, link names that merge image alt text with price text, and 24 duplicate carousel items; hard to tell products apart.

Express checkout buttons and card fields are inside iframes with unnamed frames, and the page has several empty status regions and a shortened (not fully listed) State list; harder to understand structure.
